introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours. Do ALL the tasks (Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3) specified in the question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three. Each version has three tasks: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task 3 (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the pictures 'foxandstork' and 'hareandtortoise' found on the desktop) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP TWO - TASK 1 (20 marks)**

*Figure 1 is a story typed and enclosed in a frame. Your task is to type, edit and format the text as requested.*

> **The Hare and the Tortoise** *(title)*
>
> There once was a speedy hare who bragged about how fast he could run. Tired of hearing him boast, the tortoise challenged him to a race. All the animals in the forest gathered to watch. The hare ran down the road for a while and then paused to rest. He looked back at the tortoise and cried out, "How do you expect to win this race when you are walking along at your slow, slow pace?" The hare stretched himself out alongside the road and fell asleep, thinking, "There is plenty of time to relax."
>
> The tortoise walked and walked, never ever stopping until he came to the finish line. The animals who were watching cheered so loudly for tortoise that they woke up the hare. The hare stretched, yawned and began to run again, but it was too late. Tortoise had already crossed the finish line.
>
> After being defeated by the tortoise, the hare did some soul-searching. He knew that though he had tried hard in the beginning, he was not consistent, and had grown overconfident. He was determined to undo his mistakes, and invited tortoise for another race. This time, the rabbit was careful to run the whole distance, and of course, emerged the winner.
>
> **Morale: Fast and consistent may be better than slow and steady.**
>
> Source: *https://www.kidsworldfun.com/shortstories_hareandtortoise.php*
>
> **Figure 1**

Task 1, Group Two : points imprimés 7 + 2 + 2 + 2 + (2+1+2) + 2 = 20, comme l'en-tête. Le texte de la Figure 1 est recopié tel qu'imprimé, y compris « tortoise » sans article, « the rabbit » (au lieu de la tortue) et « Morale » ; une marque parasite après « again, » est lue comme un espace. Question 2 : le nombre de mots (207 pour les trois paragraphes, 225 pour tout le cadre) est calculé par script sur ma transcription ; le compteur d'un traitement de texte peut différer de 1 ou 2 si la saisie diffère (trait d'union, ponctuation collée) et le sujet ne dit pas si le titre, la morale et la source comptent : les deux totaux sont donnés.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch any word processor installed in your PC and type all the text of Figure 1.  *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Start a word processor (for example *Start* > *Microsoft Word* > *Blank document*) and type the whole text of Figure 1: the title *The Hare and the Tortoise*, the three paragraphs, the line *Morale: Fast and consistent may be better than slow and steady.* and the line *Source: https://www.kidsworldfun.com/shortstories_hareandtortoise.php*. Press *Enter* only at the end of a paragraph, keep the spelling and the punctuation exactly as printed (including the quotation marks and the hyphen of *soul-searching*), and let the program wrap the lines.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the easiest way to count the words in the text. Hence, state the number of words in the story.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Easiest way:** let the word processor count them. The **Words** counter is displayed in the status bar at the bottom of the window; it can also be opened with *Review* > **Word Count**. To count only the story, select the three paragraphs first: the status bar then shows "selected words of total words" and the dialog gives the number for the selection. (Counting by hand is slow and error-prone.)

**Number of words:** the three paragraphs of the story contain 95 + 52 + 60 = **207 words** (the title adds 5, the morale 11 and the source line 2, so the whole text of Figure 1 has 225 words). The count was made by script on the text as typed above: the word processor counts the groups of characters separated by spaces.

questions.enonce_markdown: Separate the text within the three main paragraphs into 2 columns.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select only the three paragraphs of the story (not the title, the morale and the source line). In the *Layout* tab choose **Columns** > **Two**. The word processor puts the selected text in two newspaper-style columns (it inserts continuous section breaks before and after the selection, so the title and the last two lines stay in one column).

questions.enonce_markdown: Justify the text in the columns and increase line spacing to 1.15.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: With the text of the columns still selected: click **Justify** (*Home* tab, *Ctrl + J*), then open **Line and Paragraph Spacing** (*Home* tab, the icon with the arrows) and choose **1.15** (or *Paragraph* dialog > *Line spacing* > *Multiple* > *At* 1.15).

questions.enonce_markdown: Bold, Center and apply a font size of 16 to the title.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the title *The Hare and the Tortoise*, then in the *Home* tab: **B** (Bold, *Ctrl + B*), **Center** (*Ctrl + E*) and font size **16**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the story text and apply a serif font of size 11.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the three paragraphs of the story and choose a **serif** font (for example **Times New Roman**, Cambria or Georgia) in the font box, then the size **11** in the size box.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a Drop Cap for the first letter of the first paragraph.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Click inside the first paragraph (*There once was a speedy hare ...*). In the *Insert* tab, *Text* group, click **Drop Cap** and choose **Dropped** (or *Drop Cap Options...* > *Dropped*). The first letter, **T**, becomes a large capital letter that occupies several lines at the beginning of the paragraph.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert the image hareandtortoise (found on the desktop) at the start of the third paragraph of your text.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Click at the very beginning of the third paragraph (*After being defeated by the tortoise ...*). *Insert* tab > **Pictures** > *This Device*, open the **Desktop**, select **hareandtortoise** and click *Insert*. If the picture is too large for the column, reduce it with a corner handle so that it keeps its proportions, and set *Wrap Text* to **Square** if the text should flow around it. *[The picture file is supplied on the day; it is not in the printed paper.]*

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 1 in your working directory.
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > **Save As** > working directory, file name **Task 1**, then *Save*.
*File* > **Print** (*Ctrl + P*), 1 copy, then *Print*; attach the copy to the booklet.
